name: Pesticide Exposure
overview: Pesticides can enter the body through skin contact, inhalation, or ingestion. Quick action reduces absorption and harm.

steps.title: Move to fresh air
steps.detail: Get the person away from the sprayed area immediately.

steps.title: Remove contaminated clothing
steps.detail: Take off clothing that has pesticide on it. Cut if needed to avoid pulling over the head.

steps.title: Wash skin thoroughly
steps.detail: Rinse exposed skin with water for at least 15 minutes. Use soap when available.

steps.title: If in eyes
steps.detail: Flush eyes with clean water for 15–20 minutes. Hold eyelids open.

steps.title: If swallowed
steps.detail: Do NOT induce vomiting unless a poison control or medical professional says so. Rinse mouth with water.

when_to_seek_help: Call 911 immediately if: difficulty breathing, confusion, seizures, unconsciousness, severe vomiting, or skin that blisters. Call poison control (1-800-222-1222) for milder exposure.
prevention_tips: Wear chemical-resistant gloves, long sleeves, and pants when mixing or spraying.
Use a respirator mask (not just a dust mask) when handling chemicals.
Read the label and follow re-entry times before entering treated areas.
